rulebook: DELC Rules for Certified Child Care Centers, CCLD-0084 (OAR 414-305)

findings.requirement: The handbook must name the person with immediate responsibility for daily operation, with business address and phone number.
findings.quote: Name, business address, and business telephone number of the person(s) who has immediate responsibility for the daily operation of the center;
findings.handbook_quote: Director: Renata Okafor-Lindqvist, responsible for daily operation Business address: 2250 NE Wren Hollow Road, Salem, OR 97301 Business phone: (503) 555-0148

findings.requirement: The handbook must describe licensed capacity, ages and number of children, hours, days, months, closures, holidays, and ratios.
findings.quote: A center description including the licensed capacity, ages and number of children in care, hours, days and months of operation, closure dates and observed holidays, and staff-to-child ratios;
findings.handbook_quote: Thimbleberry Hollow is certified for 60 children. We currently care for 58 children: 8 infants, 10 toddlers, and 40 preschoolers. We are open Monday through Friday, 7:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m., all twelve months of the year.

findings.requirement: The handbook must state arrival and departure procedures, sign-in and sign-out requirements, and authorized pickup persons.
findings.quote: Arrival and departure procedures, including sign in and out requirements and individuals authorized for pick-up;
findings.handbook_quote: Please walk your child into the classroom and stay until a teacher has greeted and accepted your child. Sign your child in and out each day on the tablet at the classroom door.

findings.requirement: The handbook must explain parent responsibilities for providing current required information and what parents must provide.
findings.quote: Parent responsibilities for providing current required information and what parents are expected to provide;
findings.handbook_quote: You are responsible for keeping this information current. Please tell us right away about new phone numbers, addresses, pickup persons, allergies, medications, or health changes, and review and sign the enrollment form at least once a year.

findings.requirement: The handbook must include health policies covering toileting, diapering, handwashing, infant feeding support, bottles and pacifiers, immunization tracking, medication, repellent and sunscreen, bed linen, ill child care, exclusion, and injury response.
findings.quote: Health policies and procedures to include toileting, diaper changing and handwashing methods, support for parents feeding their infants, storage and handling of bottles and pacifiers, immunization tracking, medication administration, use of insect repellent and sunscreen, care of bed linen, care of children who are ill and exclusion criteria, and response to injuries
findings.handbook_quote: Children and staff wash hands with soap and running water on arrival, before and after eating, after toileting or diapering, after outdoor play, and after touching animals. We check diapers at least every 2 hours and change them promptly, following the procedure posted at each changing table.

findings.requirement: The handbook must state safety measures including safe sleep, monitoring sleeping infants, injury prevention, pesticides and toxic substances, animals, water activities, and prohibited substances.
findings.quote: Safety measures including safe sleep practices, monitoring of sleeping infants, injury prevention, use of pesticides and other potentially toxic substances, animals, water activities, and prohibited substances;
findings.handbook_quote: Infants are always placed on their backs to sleep, on the firm, flat mattress of their own crib. Babies who roll over on their own may stay in the position they choose.

findings.requirement: The handbook must include a plan ensuring visitors or other adults not enrolled or conditionally enrolled in the CBR do not have unsupervised access to children.
findings.quote: A plan to ensure that any visitor or other adult not enrolled or conditionally enrolled in the CBR does not have unsupervised access to children;
findings.handbook_quote: Any adult who is not enrolled in the Central Background Registry is always accompanied by a staff member and is never alone with children.

findings.requirement: The handbook must include the emergency preparedness plan.
findings.quote: Emergency preparedness plan (also see OAR 414-305-0210, Emergency Preparedness and Response);
findings.handbook_quote: Our written emergency plan covers fire, earthquake, severe weather, power outages, a lost child, a hostile intruder, and medical emergencies. We evacuate to the church parking lot next door, more than 50 feet from our building.

findings.requirement: The handbook must state the center philosophy on how children learn and develop and how it is implemented.
findings.quote: Center philosophy on how children learn and develop, and how this philosophy is implemented;
findings.handbook_quote: We believe young children learn through play, relationships, and curiosity. They grow when they choose meaningful activities, try things out, and talk about their discoveries with caring adults.

findings.requirement: The handbook must include daily schedules with planned activities, rest time, physical activity, and screen time.
findings.quote: Daily schedules that include planned activities, rest time, physical activity, and screen time;
findings.handbook_quote: Every day includes at least an hour of active physical play, indoors if the weather is unsafe. Infants and toddlers follow their own feeding and sleeping rhythms. We don't use screens with children under 2.

findings.requirement: The handbook must describe center-sponsored religious and cultural activities and how holidays are recognized.
findings.quote: Center-sponsored religious and cultural activities, if any, including how holidays will be recognized;
findings.handbook_quote: We do not hold religious activities. We celebrate our families' cultures by inviting them to share songs, foods, stories, and traditions, and we recognize holidays through books and conversations about how different families celebrate.

findings.requirement: The handbook must state meals, snacks, and food service practices including storage and handling, dietary needs and allergies, infant feeding, and food from home.
findings.quote: Meals, snacks, and food service practices including food storage and handling, children’s dietary needs and allergies, infant feeding, and food brought from the child’s home;
findings.handbook_quote: We serve breakfast, lunch, and three snacks that meet CACFP guidelines, so children never go more than 3½ hours without a meal or snack. The weekly menu is posted at the entrance.

findings.requirement: The handbook must state transportation and field trip policies including driver and vehicle requirements and supervision.
findings.quote: Transportation and field trips including driver and vehicle requirements and supervision;
findings.handbook_quote: For trips that need driving, we use our center van. Drivers are staff at least 21 years old with a valid license, a clean driving record, and first aid and CPR training.

findings.requirement: The handbook must include the behavior and guidance policy.
findings.quote: (m) Transportation and field trips including driver and vehicle requirements and supervision; (n) Behavior and guidance policies;
findings.handbook_quote: We use positive guidance to help children learn self-control and respect for others: clear expectations, redirection, problem-solving together, and praise for kind choices.

findings.requirement: The handbook must explain how staff proceed if a child displays inappropriate behaviors that could endanger themselves or others.
findings.quote: How staff must proceed if a child is displaying inappropriate behaviors that could endanger themselves or the safety of others;
findings.handbook_quote: If a child's behavior could hurt themselves or others, a teacher moves other children away, stays calm and close, and uses words and comfort to help the child settle.

findings.requirement: The handbook must describe communication methods, notifications, and how parent grievances, questions, or concerns are handled.
findings.quote: Communication methods and notifications, including how parent grievances, questions, or concerns are handled by the center;
findings.handbook_quote: We share news through our family app, a monthly newsletter, and daily written reports for infants and toddlers. Conferences are held twice a year, or anytime you ask.

findings.requirement: The handbook must state prevention of and duty to report suspected child abuse and neglect.
findings.quote: Prevention of and duty to report suspected child abuse and neglect;
findings.handbook_quote: Every staff member is a mandatory reporter and must report any suspicion of abuse or neglect immediately to the Oregon Child Abuse Hotline (1-855-503-7233), DHS Child Welfare, or law enforcement.

findings.requirement: The handbook must describe evening and night care if provided.
findings.quote: Evening and night care, if provided;
findings.note: Beam marked this as covered, but the words it quoted don't appear in your handbook exactly as written (it may have joined two lines, such as two rows of a table).

findings.requirement: The handbook must explain how to view inspection reports, access DELC website and center certification rules, and contact CCLD and the child abuse and neglect hotline.
findings.quote: How to view inspection reports, access the Department of Early Learning and Care website and center certification rules, and contact CCLD and child abuse and neglect hotline;
findings.handbook_quote: Our most recent CCLD inspection report and the Oregon rules for certified child care centers are available on request at the front desk. Visit the Department of Early Learning and Care at www.oregonearlylearning.com or call 1-800-556-6616.

findings.requirement: The handbook must advise parents that they can access information about child care providers on the child care safety portal.
findings.quote: A statement advising parents that they can access information about child care providers on the child care safety portal.
findings.handbook_quote: You can also look up information about any child care provider, including us, on Oregon's child care safety portal.

findings.requirement: The handbook must include the suspension and expulsion prevention policy.
findings.quote: Suspension and expulsion prevention policy (OAR 414-305-0750).
findings.handbook_quote: Our goal is for every child to stay with us. When a teacher has ongoing concerns about a child's behavior, or right after any unsafe incident, the teacher asks the director for support.

findings.requirement: The center must complete an individualized assessment when aware a child with specific needs has applied or is in care, documenting needed modifications.
findings.quote: a certified child care center must complete an individualized assessment whenever the center becomes aware that a child with specific needs has either applied for enrollment or is already in care at the center.
findings.handbook_quote: When we learn that a child with specific needs has applied or is enrolled, we complete an individualized assessment with the family to identify reasonable changes to our space, policies, and practices.
findings.explanation: The handbook describes the assessment but does not say it is documented for each child with the required descriptions of changes.
findings.fix: When we learn that a child with specific needs has applied or is enrolled, we complete an individualized assessment with the family and document it for that child. The documentation describes changes we make or cannot reasonably make to our space, policies, and practices, and any safety concerns.

findings.requirement: The center must practice evacuation drills monthly and one other emergency plan aspect every other month.
findings.quote: A certified child care center must practice evacuation drills monthly and one other aspect of the emergency plan every other month that:
findings.handbook_quote: We practice a fire evacuation drill every month, and every other month we also practice another part of our plan, such as an earthquake drill, shelter-in-place, or lockdown.

findings.requirement: The center must comply with Oregon Health Authority immunization rules for children.
findings.quote: A certified child care center must comply with Oregon Health Authority’s administrative rules (see OAR 333-050-0040) relating to the immunization of children.
findings.handbook_quote: We track every child's immunizations as Oregon Health Authority rules require and remind you when an update is due.

findings.requirement: Parent permission for a field trip must be specific with dates, times, and locations for each field trip.
findings.quote: A certified child care center must have parent permission prior to a field trip or other activity away from the immediate neighborhood. Field trip permission must be specific with dates, times, and locations for each field trip.
findings.handbook_quote: Before each trip, we ask you to sign a permission slip listing that trip's date, times, and location.

findings.requirement: A child may only be released to a parent or another person named and identified by the parent, with identification if not known to staff.
findings.quote: A certified child care center may only release a child to a parent or another person named and identified by the parent(s). A person picking up the child must show identification if not known to staff.
findings.handbook_quote: We release children only to parents and to adults you have named on your child's authorized pickup list. Anyone we don't know must show photo identification.

findings.requirement: Child and personnel records must be kept confidential and available only to necessary personnel, the child's parents, and CCLD staff.
findings.quote: A certified child care center must keep child and personnel records confidential and only available to personnel as necessary, the individual child's parents, and CCLD staff.
findings.handbook_quote: Your child's records are confidential and available only to staff who need them, to you as your child's parent, and to CCLD staff.

findings.requirement: Custodial parents have access to all child care areas upon notifying any staff member during hours of operation and without advance notice.
findings.quote: A notice that custodial parents have access to all child care areas upon notifying any staff member of their presence during the hours of operation and without advance notice;
findings.handbook_quote: Custodial parents may visit all child care areas at any time during our hours, without advance notice. Just let any staff member know you are here.

findings.requirement: The center must post information on how to report a complaint to CCLD regarding certification requirements.
findings.quote: Information on how to report a complaint to CCLD regarding certification requirements;
findings.handbook_quote: Visit the Department of Early Learning and Care at www.oregonearlylearning.com or call 1-800-556-6616 to read the rules, reach CCLD, or report a complaint.

findings.requirement: Any staff member who suspects child abuse or neglect must report immediately to the Oregon Child Abuse Hotline, DHS Child Welfare, or law enforcement.
findings.quote: Any staff member who has reason to believe a child has been abused or neglected is required to report the matter immediately to the Oregon Child Abuse Hotline
findings.handbook_quote: Every staff member is a mandatory reporter and must report any suspicion of abuse or neglect immediately to the Oregon Child Abuse Hotline (1-855-503-7233), DHS Child Welfare, or law enforcement.

findings.requirement: Centers initially licensed after July 15, 2001 must use Table 3A ratios and group sizes, such as 1:4 for infants and 1:15 for school-age children.
findings.quote: All certified child care centers with initial certification after July 15, 2001, must comply with staff-to-child ratios and group size in Table 3A.
findings.handbook_quote: In the Fern Room, two teachers care for no more than 10 toddlers, which keeps us at one teacher for every five children.

findings.requirement: Staff must supervise children within sight and sound without relying on audio or video monitoring devices, except as specified.
findings.quote: Be within sight and sound, without relying on audio or video monitoring devices, except as specified in OAR 414-305-0500(4).
findings.handbook_quote: Teachers supervise children within sight and sound and never rely on baby monitors or cameras in place of a teacher in the room.

findings.requirement: The center must not provide care for a child under six weeks of age.
findings.quote: A certified child care center must not provide care for a child under six weeks of age.
findings.handbook_quote: We are a certified child care center for children from 6 weeks through 5 years old.

findings.requirement: Infants must be placed on their backs on a flat, firm, non-inclined surface for sleeping.
findings.quote: Infants must be placed on their backs on a flat, firm, non-inclined surface for sleeping.
findings.handbook_quote: Infants are always placed on their backs to sleep, on the firm, flat mattress of their own crib.

findings.requirement: The center must not use or threaten prohibited discipline, including corporal punishment, isolation, food withdrawal, or humiliation.
findings.quote: A certified child care center must not use or threaten to use any of the following prohibited actions even if requested or agreed to by parents:
findings.handbook_quote: We never hit, spank, shake, or handle a child roughly; never isolate a child in a closed or dark space; never withhold or force food, rest, or toileting; never yell harshly, shame, or tease; and never punish toileting accidents, even if a parent asks us to.

findings.requirement: Physical restraint may only be used when a child's safety or others' safety is threatened, gently and for the minimum time necessary.
findings.quote: Physical restraint must only be used if a child's safety or the safety of others is threatened and must be: (a) Limited to holding a child as gently as possible to accomplish restraint;
findings.handbook_quote: Physical restraint is used only when someone's safety is threatened, and only as a gentle hold for the shortest time needed.

findings.requirement: The center must not exceed licensed capacity at any time, including children in care away from the center.
findings.quote: A certified child care center must not exceed its licensed capacity at any time, including the total number of children in care both at and away from the center.

findings.requirement: The center must provide at least 35 square feet of activity space per child.
findings.quote: A certified child care center must have a minimum of 35 square feet of activity space per child.
findings.handbook_quote: Each classroom has at least 35 square feet of activity space per child.

findings.requirement: The center must provide at least 75 square feet of outdoor activity space per child using the space at one time.
findings.quote: A certified child care center must provide an outdoor activity space of no less than 75 square feet for each child using the space at one time
findings.handbook_quote: our playground has more than 75 square feet for each child using it at one time.

findings.requirement: The center must not accept a child diagnosed as having or being a carrier of a child care restrictable disease without written approval.
findings.quote: (a) Is diagnosed as having or being a carrier of a child care restrictable disease, as defined in Oregon Health Authority administrative rules, except with the written approval
findings.handbook_quote: A child with a restrictable disease may return only with written approval from a health care provider or public health.

findings.requirement: Any injury that may need physician evaluation or impact to a child's head must be reported to parents immediately and documented.
findings.quote: Any injury that may need evaluation by a physician or impact to a child’s head must be reported to the child’s parent(s) immediately and documented.
findings.handbook_quote: We call you immediately for any bump to the head or any injury that may need a doctor.

findings.requirement: Before giving medication, the center must have signed, dated, written parent authorization on file.
findings.quote: Have a signed, dated, written authorization by the parent(s) on file (also see OAR 414-305-0230, Parental Permissions);
findings.handbook_quote: Before we give any medicine, prescription or over-the-counter, you must complete and sign a dated medication authorization form for that medicine.

findings.requirement: Children in care more than 3.5 consecutive hours must be served a meal or snack every 3.5 hours.
findings.quote: Children in care for more than 3 ½ consecutive hours must be served a meal or snack every 3 ½ hours;
findings.handbook_quote: We serve breakfast, lunch, and three snacks that meet CACFP guidelines, so children never go more than 3½ hours without a meal or snack.

findings.requirement: Children must never be left unattended inside or outside of a vehicle.
findings.quote: A certified child care center must never leave children unattended inside or outside of a vehicle.
findings.handbook_quote: children are never left unattended inside or outside a vehicle.

findings.requirement: Written parent permission is required before engaging in any swimming activities.
findings.quote: A certified child care center must have written permission from each child’s parent before engaging in any swimming activities.
findings.handbook_quote: We do not offer swimming; if we ever did, we would first get your written permission and share our safety plan.

findings.requirement: Parents must be informed of any animals on the premises by a clearly viewed notice, policy handbook, parent flier, or enrollment statement.
findings.quote: A certified child care center must inform parents of any animals on the premises by a clearly viewed notice or bulletin, policy handbook, parent flier, or a statement included on the enrollment form
findings.handbook_quote: The Cedar Room has two guinea pigs in a covered cage. Children may help feed them with a teacher beside them.

findings.requirement: A center must be approved by CCLD before providing night care.
findings.quote: A certified child care center must be approved by CCLD to provide night care, as defined in 414-305-0100(32).

findings.requirement: Active play time for children in care more than six hours
findings.quote: Programs that operate more than 6 hours a day must provide 90 minutes of active play for children preschool age and older or 60 minutes of active play for infants and toddlers (30 minutes of which may be moderate to vigorous indoor activities).
findings.handbook_quote: Every day includes at least an hour of active physical play, indoors if the weather is unsafe.
findings.explanation: The center is open more than six hours a day, so preschoolers need 90 minutes of active play, but the handbook promises only at least an hour.
findings.fix: Every day includes at least 90 minutes of active play for preschoolers and 60 minutes for infants and toddlers, with outdoor play whenever weather and air quality are safe. If outdoor play is not safe, up to 30 minutes may be moderate to vigorous indoor activity.

summary: The handbook covers nearly all required policies and rules. One policy item needs documentation details added, and one activity-time statement should be updated to match the 90-minute requirement.
